mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__drou.mechanism: In a national census of post-tsunami mangrove planting sites in Sri Lanka, seedlings and propagules planted in the higher intertidal zone of the dry and arid zones suffered from drought and high irradiance [ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_2].
mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__drou.conditionality: This is a single observational source; it describes stress at poorly sited plantings rather than measuring how much drought reduced survival, and it points to planting position along the tidal gradient as the controlling factor.

mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__extr.mechanism: Compilers judge mangrove regeneration in Senegal as coping well with local rainstorms and mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh as coping well with local thunderstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1442_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4300_2019_local_thunderstorm].
mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__extr.conditionality: Both units are practitioner judgements of good coping, with no observed damage behind the threat class.

mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__floo.mechanism: Flooding was among the stress factors observed at all planted mangrove sites in a national census in Sri Lanka, alongside drought, smothering, high irradiance, browsing and cattle trampling [ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_3]. In Vietnam's Bac Lieu province mangrove replanting was less successful, mostly because of heavy storms and flooding and poor planting techniques [ev_frmg_vnppar_5].
mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__floo.conditionality: Compilers rate mangrove regeneration in Senegal as coping well with river floods, mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh as coping well with storm surge and mangrove buffers in the Philippines as coping very well [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1442_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_4300_2019_storm_surge_coastal_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_578_2016_storm_surge_coastal_flood], so these ratings are practitioner judgements of slight threat; the Sri Lankan observation does not separate flooding from the other stresses. The Bac Lieu account, relayed by an independent evaluation, likewise does not separate flooding from storms and poor planting technique, and it concerns newly planted stands that failed to establish rather than an established forest [ev_frmg_vnppar_5]. The threat falls on the establishment window and on siting.

mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__sedi.mechanism: A review reports, citing earlier field and laboratory work second-hand, that rapid sedimentation and excess leaf litter can cause delayed mortality of mangrove trees by smothering the above-ground aerial roots [ev_establishment_survival_gijsman21_1].
mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__sedi.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity for restored mangroves: it is a single second-hand review statement about existing mangrove forests, with no magnitude and no measured finding on planted or regenerating stands. A second independent source, or a measured finding on restoration sites, is what is missing; the row should not be read as saying restoration works are undamaged by sedimentation. Part of the effect is off-site rather than on the adopting farm.

mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__wate.mechanism: In Sri Lanka, mangrove seedlings and propagules planted in the low intertidal zone of the wet zone were exposed to long-term submergence due to heavy rains [ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_1].
mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__wate.conditionality: This is a single observational source that does not quantify the resulting losses; the exposure is linked to the planting position along the tidal gradient, a siting error rather than a property of the practice.

mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__wind.mechanism: Mangrove tree damage rises rapidly once tropical-cyclone winds exceed 130 km/h, and extreme events with very high water levels and wind speeds may severely damage or destroy mangrove areas, leaving them less able to reduce surge [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_establishment_survival_mcivor12_1]. In Florida the 2005 Hurricane Wilma was estimated to have initially destroyed 1250 ha of mangroves, and frequent hurricanes have changed some mangrove stands to mudflats [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1]. In Vietnam's Bac Lieu province mangrove replanting was less successful, mostly because of heavy storms and flooding and poor planting techniques, and project staff told the evaluation mission that a severe storm arriving before the roots could take a firm hold in the sand would take out enough seedlings to require yet another replanting [ev_frmg_vnppar_6, ev_frmg_vnppar_7]. On the Bangladesh coast, project staff report that cyclonic shocks caused severe damages of both the Sundarbans and planted mangroves through species loss and creating large gaps [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_4].
mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__wind.conditionality: Compilers judge mangrove regeneration in Senegal as coping well with local windstorms and mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh as coping moderately with tropical storms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1442_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4300_2019_tropical_storm]. The review units, including the Florida loss estimate, are cited findings for existing mangrove forests, not measurements on restored stands [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_establishment_survival_mcivor12_1, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1]. Only the Vietnam and Bangladesh accounts concern planted stands, and none is a measurement: the Vietnam units are evaluator and project-staff reports, and the Bac Lieu losses mix storms, flooding and poor planting technique [ev_frmg_vnppar_6, ev_frmg_vnppar_7]; the Bangladesh statement comes from staff of the implementing project, gives no extent of the loss, and its 'severe' describes the damage, not the storm [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_4]. The exposure is sharpest before the roots take hold, so the threat to an investment sits in the establishment years.

mangrove_restoration__biodiversity_prior.mechanism: In a global meta-analysis of mostly planted mangrove restoration, restored mangroves exhibit higher levels of crab production and diversity than degraded mangroves (RR′ = 0.80, 95% CIs = 0.64 to 0.97) [ev_biodiversity_outcome_su21_1]. A WOCAT mangrove afforestation sheet from Bangladesh reports that the plantation site supports habitats for birds and crabs and develops suitable habitats for wildlife and fish [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4300_2019_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4300_2019_habitat_diversity]. In Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta an independent evaluation relays that forest cover in the protection zones increased from around 50 percent in 2000 to 96 percent in 2007 as a result of the project, and that the zones around mangrove roots protected from the violence of the sea created breeding grounds for fish and shellfish, with sea crabs and shellfish re-appearing in some places and increasing in others [ev_frmg_vnppar_3, ev_frmg_vnppar_4].
mangrove_restoration__biodiversity_prior.conditionality: The same meta-analysis found no major difference in crab or fish production and diversity between restored mangroves and unvegetated tidal flats, and its metric merges production with diversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_su21_2], so the gain depends on the comparison: it holds against degraded mangrove, not against the open tidal flat. The Bangladesh entries are compiler ratings, not measurements. The Vietnam cover figure is before-and-after project data with no counterfactual, which stakeholders described as only partly attributable to the project; it includes casuarina windbreak planting and protection of existing forest, and it is cover rather than a count of species [ev_frmg_vnppar_3]. The return of crabs and shellfish is an anecdotal observation, and it came with protection contracts given to smallholders as well as the replanting [ev_frmg_vnppar_4].

mangrove_restoration__carbon_sequestrati.mechanism: Planted mangroves deliver carbon removals as the growing trees store carbon in biomass and soil: a global review of forest landscape restoration finds mangrove tree restoration the second most efficient type at removing CO2, at up to 23.1 t CO2 per hectare per year in the first 20 years and 10.5 over the following 40 years [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_2, ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_4]. A mangrove meta-analysis also finds higher carbon sequestration in restored mangroves than in unvegetated tidal flats (RR′ = 0.64, 95% CIs = 0.35 to 0.94) [ev_carbon_sequestration_su21_1]. In Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta forest cover in the protection zones increased from around 50 percent in 2000 to 96 percent in 2007 as a result of the project, which enters here as cover rather than a carbon stock [ev_frmg_vnppar_3].
mangrove_restoration__carbon_sequestrati.conditionality: The removal-rate review covers active planting only, and its text and table give slightly different later-period rates [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_4]; the meta-analysis reports publication bias for carbon sequestration against tidal flats [ev_carbon_sequestration_su21_1]. The Vietnam cover figure is project before-and-after data with no counterfactual, only partly attributable to the project according to stakeholders, and it mixes replanting with casuarina windbreaks and protection of existing forest [ev_frmg_vnppar_3]. A project-experience paper from coastal Bangladesh adds a project-total claim of the carbon its coastal afforestation was arranged to absorb each year, with no per-hectare rate or method; the extraction flags the implied rate as implausible for young mangrove plantation, so the unit carries no size and does not set the strength [ev_carbon_sequestration_ahammad13_3]. The rates are those of stands that established; a planting that washes out sequesters nothing.

mangrove_restoration__carbon_sequestrati.mechanism: In lower-income settings the row rests on Bangladesh alone: the WOCAT compiler for mangrove afforestation rates below-ground soil organic matter as increased, a component proxy for sequestration [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_4300_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C], and a project-experience paper reports that the project's coastal afforestation, new mangrove plantation on newly accreted char lands, made mitigation arrangements to absorb carbon annually [ev_carbon_sequestration_ahammad13_3].
mangrove_restoration__carbon_sequestrati.conditionality: Neither unit measures a removal rate. The WOCAT entry is a compiler rating of soil organic matter, not of carbon in the trees [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_4300_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C]. The project paper is written by staff of the implementing project, states a project-total projection with no per-hectare rate, method or monitoring, and the extraction flags its implied rate as implausible for young plantation, so it gives a direction but no size [ev_carbon_sequestration_ahammad13_3]. Measured removal rates for planted mangroves come from outside this income scope; a lower-income project would need its own stock or growth measurements to claim a carbon size.

mangrove_restoration__cost_per_hectare_r.mechanism: These are per-hectare costs of establishing mangroves, mostly by planting. Compiler-entered establishment costs are 427.38 USD/ha on a WOCAT sheet from Bangladesh and 150.00 USD/ha from the Philippines [ev_project_cost_wocat_4300_2019_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_578_2016_establishment]. Cited reforestation costs are US$946/ha in Thailand and US$211/ha for community-supported reforestation in the Philippines [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_3, ev_project_cost_hernmel17_4]; a community project in northern Viet Nam put the present-value cost to create one hectare of mangrove at 843 US dollars [ev_project_cost_ifrc11_1]. A global meta-analysis gives a median total restoration cost of 1,097.16 USD/ha within a range of 23.22 to 371,326.75 USD/ha [ev_project_cost_su21_1], a global cost-carbon study uses an average of US$4368 per hectare [ev_project_cost_jakovac20_3], and a World Bank study models a national mean of 7,700 USD/ha for Bangladesh [ev_project_cost_wbmang25_1].
mangrove_restoration__cost_per_hectare_r.conditionality: The figures rest on different cost bases. The Mexican value, US$94.68/ha, was set by budget availability under a subsidy programme rather than being a full cost, and the authors argue it was insufficient for success [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_1]; several cited figures state no price year; and the meta-analysis range runs from direct propagule dibbing at the low end to very costly projects [ev_project_cost_su21_1]. WOCAT costs are compiler entries converted from local currency, and the World Bank figure is a value transfer from a cost function rather than an observed project cost [ev_project_cost_wbmang25_1].

mangrove_restoration__cost_per_hectare_r.mechanism: In lower-middle-income settings the costs run from US$211/ha for community-supported mangrove reforestation in the Philippines and a compiler-entered 427.38 USD/ha for mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh, through US$990.96/ha cited for reforestation in Vietnam, to a modelled national mean of 7,700 USD/ha for mangrove restoration in Bangladesh [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_4, ev_project_cost_wocat_4300_2019_establishment, ev_project_cost_hernmel17_5, ev_project_cost_wbmang25_1].
mangrove_restoration__cost_per_hectare_r.conditionality: The Philippine figure excludes preliminary and maintenance activities, which raise it to US$1,156.52/ha [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_5], so figures that omit them understate full cost. The Vietnam value is a citation of the IFRC evaluation with no stated price year, the Bangladesh WOCAT value is a compiler entry converted from local currency, and the 7,700 USD/ha mean is a modelled value transfer from grey literature, far above the observed community-supported planting costs [ev_project_cost_wbmang25_1].

mangrove_restoration__cost_per_hectare_r.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the reported costs are US$946/ha cited for mangrove reforestation in Thailand, 843 US dollars at present value to create one hectare of mangrove in a community project in northern Viet Nam, a compiler-entered 150.00 USD/ha for mangrove buffers in the Philippines, and US$94.68/ha allocated per hectare in Tabasco, Mexico [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_3, ev_project_cost_ifrc11_1, ev_project_cost_wocat_578_2016_establishment, ev_project_cost_hernmel17_1].
mangrove_restoration__cost_per_hectare_r.conditionality: The lowest value is not a full cost: the Mexican amount was determined according to budget availability and the authors argue it was insufficient for success [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_1]. The Viet Nam figure is a present value from an implementer-commissioned evaluation, the Thai figure is a citation with no stated price year, and the Philippine figure is a compiler entry converted from local currency [ev_project_cost_ifrc11_1, ev_project_cost_hernmel17_3, ev_project_cost_wocat_578_2016_establishment].

mangrove_restoration__cost_per_tco2e_avo.mechanism: A global spatial cost-carbon model estimates the break-even carbon price at which carbon payments would cover land opportunity and restoration costs, and finds that carbon prices between 4.5 and 18.0 US$ per tCO2 could support the restoration of 90% of deforested mangroves [ev_project_cost_jakovac20_1].
mangrove_restoration__cost_per_tco2e_avo.conditionality: This is a modelled break-even price from a single global study with no country context, not an observed project cost per tonne; it depends on the assumed opportunity and restoration costs and on the share of carbon credited, and it assumes the restored stands establish.

mangrove_restoration__cost_reduction.mechanism: The only unit is a project cited second-hand from a Tabasco, Mexico, report, where 50 ha of black mangrove were reforested successfully at a full per-hectare cost covering sanitation, dredging, soil conservation works, ridge restoration, staff training, plant production, transplanting and monitoring [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_2].
mangrove_restoration__cost_reduction.conditionality: This is a description of what restoration cost, not a measured saving, so no direction or class is stated for cost reduction. It is a single second-hand project report from an upper-middle-income setting; a second independent source or a measured cost comparison is what is missing, and the source's printed per-hectare value could not be used as a magnitude.

mangrove_restoration__flood__all.mechanism: The evidence here gives a direction but no size. Of the mangrove restoration projects reviewed globally, 50% state that the habitat provides improved protection from storm events [ev_frmg_nara16_5], and a second-hand reading of an economic model for coastal districts of northern Vietnam reports that restoration scenarios have even higher cost-benefit ratios when the avoided maintenance cost of the sea dike system, protected from coastal storm surges by the mangroves, is included [ev_frmg_erw09_2].
mangrove_restoration__flood__all.conditionality: No unit here measures how far a planted stand lowers flood water or waves. The 50% counts projects that report a benefit, self-reported rather than measured; and the Vietnam dike-cost result is a model read second-hand from the original study, which the citing author does not describe further [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2]. The protection these units describe falls on the coast and the sea dike behind the stand - avoided storm damage and avoided dike maintenance that accrue to society at large, not income for the household that plants or tends the mangroves [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2].

mangrove_restoration__flood__all__income.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the row holds two units: the compiler for mangrove buffers in the Philippines rates flood impacts as decreased [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts], and a second-hand reading of an economic model for coastal districts of northern Vietnam reports that restoration scenarios have even higher cost-benefit ratios when the avoided maintenance cost of the sea dike system, protected from coastal storm surges by the mangroves, is included [ev_frmg_erw09_2].
mangrove_restoration__flood__all__income.conditionality: Neither unit measures flood levels or wave reduction behind a planted stand: the Philippine unit is a compiler rating and the Vietnam unit a model result cited second-hand [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts, ev_frmg_erw09_2]. The Vietnam value is the avoided upkeep of a public sea dike, a saving to society rather than income reaching the households working the coast [ev_frmg_erw09_2].

mangrove_restoration__flood_hazard.mechanism: The moderate strength rests on the only sized unit, a review cited by a Bhitarkanika study that reports a 20–30% reduction in repair and maintenance costs of sea-dyke systems depending on the width of mangrove stand in front of the dyke (Adger et al. 1997) [ev_avoided_damage_value_badola05_10]. Of the mangrove restoration projects reviewed globally, 50% state that the habitat provides improved protection from storm events [ev_frmg_nara16_5], and a second-hand reading of an economic model for coastal districts of northern Vietnam reports that restoration scenarios have even higher cost-benefit ratios when the avoided maintenance cost of the sea dike system, protected from coastal storm surges by the mangroves, is included [ev_frmg_erw09_2].
mangrove_restoration__flood_hazard.conditionality: No unit here measures how far a planted stand lowers flood water or waves. The 50% counts projects that report a benefit, self-reported rather than measured; and the Vietnam dike-cost result is a model read second-hand from the original study, which the citing author does not describe further [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2]. The protection these units describe falls on the coast and the sea dike behind the stand - avoided storm damage and avoided dike maintenance that accrue to society at large, not income for the household that plants or tends the mangroves [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2]. The dyke-cost reduction is cited second-hand from a Vietnam valuation of mangrove restoration, its quote does not say whether the stand was planted or existing, and the saving is avoided upkeep of a public sea dyke, a benefit to society rather than to the households working the coast [ev_avoided_damage_value_badola05_10].

mangrove_restoration__flood_hazard__inco.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the row holds a compiler rating and dyke-cost findings: the compiler for mangrove buffers in the Philippines rates flood impacts as decreased [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts], and a second-hand reading of an economic model for coastal districts of northern Vietnam reports that restoration scenarios have even higher cost-benefit ratios when the avoided maintenance cost of the sea dike system, protected from coastal storm surges by the mangroves, is included [ev_frmg_erw09_2]. A review cited by a Bhitarkanika study reports a 20–30% reduction in repair and maintenance costs of sea-dyke systems depending on the width of mangrove stand in front of the dyke (Adger et al. 1997) [ev_avoided_damage_value_badola05_10].
mangrove_restoration__flood_hazard__inco.conditionality: Neither unit measures flood levels or wave reduction behind a planted stand: the Philippine unit is a compiler rating and the Vietnam unit a model result cited second-hand [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts, ev_frmg_erw09_2]. The Vietnam value is the avoided upkeep of a public sea dike, a saving to society rather than income reaching the households working the coast [ev_frmg_erw09_2]. The dyke-cost reduction is cited second-hand from a Vietnam valuation of mangrove restoration, its quote does not say whether the stand was planted or existing, and the saving is avoided upkeep of a public sea dyke, a benefit to society rather than to the households working the coast [ev_avoided_damage_value_badola05_10].

mangrove_restoration__food_insecurity.mechanism: The only food-security evidence for mangrove planting comes from practitioner records of the technology: in Senegal the WOCAT compiler rates food security and self-sufficiency under mangrove regeneration as improved, at +2 on the WOCAT impact scale [ev_food_security_wocat_1442_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency], and in Bangladesh the compiler for mangrove afforestation against land degradation rates the risk of production failure as decreased, at +1 [ev_food_security_wocat_4300_2019_risk_of_production_failure]. Both point the same way, towards more secure food supply for the people using the restored coast.
mangrove_restoration__food_insecurity.conditionality: Both units are compiler ratings on the WOCAT scale, not measurements of food availability, diets or hunger, and neither says through which product or harvest the gain arrives. The Bangladesh rating is about the risk of production failure, a step removed from household food security itself. No study here compares food security with and without mangrove restoration, so the direction rests on practitioner judgement in a single site per country.

mangrove_restoration__production_gap.mechanism: The only evidence is a WOCAT sheet on mangrove regeneration in Senegal whose compiler rates crop production as increased, at the top of the WOCAT impact scale [ev_crop_yield_wocat_1442_2011_crop_production]; the sheet does not state the pathway.
mangrove_restoration__production_gap.conditionality: No class is stated: a single compiler rating is not a measurement, and no mechanism linking mangrove regeneration to crop output is given. A second independent source or a measured yield finding is what is missing before this cell can say whether mangrove regeneration narrows the production gap.

mangrove_restoration__recurrent_cost.mechanism: Recurrent costs are compiler-entered annual maintenance costs for mangrove plantations on WOCAT sheets: 241.07 USD per hectare per year for mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh and 20.00 for mangrove buffers in the Philippines [ev_project_cost_wocat_4300_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_578_2016_maintenance].
mangrove_restoration__recurrent_cost.conditionality: Both are WOCAT compiler entries converted from local currency and they differ widely; only the Bangladesh figure falls in the lower-middle-income band used for the class, and neither sheet itemises the maintenance tasks.

mangrove_restoration__rural_poverty.mechanism: Mangrove planting reaches people mainly through aquatic products, and the returns on the planting itself are reported as benefit-cost appraisals. In northern Viet Nam mangroves had a positive impact on additional income for coastal communities through an increase in per hectare yield of aquaculture products such as shells and oyster by 209-789 per cent [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1] - value that accrues to the households harvesting them - and the project's cost-benefit analysis gives commune benefit-cost ratios of 3.06 to 68.92 excluding ecological benefits and 28.86 to 104.96 including them [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2]. A global meta-analysis of mangrove restoration reports benefit-cost ratios of 10.50 to 6.83 across discount rates when summing benefits by ecosystem service, and 3.36 to 2.19 using the mean total economic benefit [ev_economic_return_su21_1]; a cited study concludes that the benefits of mangrove reforestation projects outweigh their costs [ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1]. A World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh models livelihood benefits of mangrove restoration at 3,700 to 86,000 USD per hectare, with regional means of 22,039 to 30,330 USD per hectare [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. A second-hand reading of an economic model for three coastal districts of northern Vietnam finds mangrove restoration desirable from an economic perspective based solely on the direct benefits of use by local communities [ev_frmg_erw09_1], and on Mexico's Gulf coast the mangrove reforestation investments at both pilot sites had positive net present values at all three discount rates considered [ev_frmg_mxicr_1]. An ex-ante appraisal for coastal Bangladesh projects that silvofishery systems combining mangrove or nypa planting with shrimp or crab culture, on land cleared for shrimp and salt farms, pay the landowner in the end: in the stable stage, all the silvofishery practices became profitable both financially and economically [ev_economic_return_rahman18_6].
mangrove_restoration__rural_poverty.conditionality: Nothing here observes household income or poverty against a counterfactual: the outcome is reached through proxies - economic return and reported income gains - and the strongest numbers are project appraisals rather than measured welfare. The 209-789 per cent is a yield increase of aquaculture products, not an income change [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1]. The Viet Nam ratios come from an evaluation commissioned by the implementer, model costs and benefits forward, and the higher ratios include ecological benefits the source says had yet to materialise [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2]; the meta-analysis pools unpaired benefit and cost samples, mostly from East and Southeast Asian planting projects [ev_economic_return_su21_1]; the Bangladesh livelihood values are modelled present values transferred from a global valuation meta-regression, not observed income, and come from grey literature [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. The Vietnam model is cited second-hand and described by the citing author as preliminary [ev_frmg_erw09_1]. The Mexico result is the project's own completion report, its benefits projected forward from planting on former cattle pasture rather than observed, with coastal protection and carbon not valued [ev_frmg_mxicr_1]. The review finding is a conclusion cited from another study [ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1]. The breakwater cost comparisons are kept out of the direction because the saving goes to society, not to households: mangrove restoration projects reported a median cost of US$0.1 per square metre (range 0.05–6.43) and an average replacement cost ratio of 5 (95% CI 3.1–6.9) against submerged breakwaters giving the same wave reduction, and depending on the water depth, mangrove projects in Vietnam can be three to five times cheaper than a breakwater [ev_frmg_nara16_3, ev_frmg_nara16_4]. That comparison assumed far lower breakwater construction costs in Vietnam than in Europe or the USA, applies only to small waves, and the authors note such defences are not always cost effective [ev_frmg_nara16_4]. A Mexican figure is kept out of the direction because its value goes to society, not to households: the cost-benefit table for the Gulf-coast pilot sites attributes $50,866 pesos/ha/year of improved water quantity and quality to each hectare of reforested mangrove [ev_mgM_mxicr_1]. It is a model input, not a measurement at the sites: the completion report says the per-hectare values come from an earlier Mexican valuation study, updated, and the report is the lender's own self-evaluation. The same table shows how little the stand itself pays its neighbours: forest products are valued at $98 pesos/ha/year, against $20,031 pesos/ha/year for improved fisheries habitat, so any income case rests on the water and fishery services rather than on anything harvested from the trees. The Bangladesh silvofishery appraisal is a projection: nothing in it was implemented or measured, yields are borrowed from other countries' models, and its returns belong to the combined planting-and-aquaculture system, not to the trees alone, so the credit goes to the bundle rather than to mangrove planting as such [ev_economic_return_rahman18_6]. It also projects a loss for landowners first, a stated harm counted against the practice: when direct financial benefits and costs were in consideration, the BCR was slightly above 1.00 only in the crab system during the establishment phase, the other systems were losing concerns (BCR < 1.00) for the landowners in the initial phase, and the mangrove-shrimp and bio-filter systems still remained below 1.00. Its headline ratios, 2.33 for mangrove-shrimp, 1.80 for nypa-shrimp and 1.40 for the bio-filter on a 35-year horizon, are read as economic ratios that include environmental benefits to society, so they are held out of this household-poverty class [ev_economic_return_rahman18_1, ev_economic_return_rahman18_2, ev_economic_return_rahman18_3]. A review's statement, from the Global Commission on Adaptation, that the benefits of mangrove protection and restoration are up to 10 times greater than their costs is held out for the same reason, and because it pools protection of standing forest with restoration [ev_economic_return_seddon21_12].

mangrove_restoration__rural_poverty__inc.mechanism: The upper-middle-income units are appraisals of mangrove planting in Viet Nam and Mexico. In northern Viet Nam mangroves had a positive impact on additional income for coastal communities through an increase in per hectare yield of aquaculture products such as shells and oyster by 209-789 per cent, value that accrues to the households harvesting them [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1], and the project's cost-benefit analysis gives commune benefit-cost ratios of 3.06 to 68.92 excluding ecological benefits and 28.86 to 104.96 including them [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2]. A second-hand reading of an economic model for three coastal districts of northern Vietnam finds mangrove restoration desirable based solely on the direct benefits of use by local communities [ev_frmg_erw09_1], and on Mexico's Gulf coast the mangrove reforestation investments at both pilot sites had positive net present values at all three discount rates considered [ev_frmg_mxicr_1].
